author: Kartik Soni
description: Comprehensive CIS-aligned security baseline for Ubuntu/Debian Linux systems

checks.title: Verify UID 0 is assigned exclusively to the root account
checks.description: No account other than root should have UID 0 to prevent unauthorized superuser access.

checks.title: Verify no accounts have empty password fields
checks.description: Accounts with empty password hashes in /etc/shadow allow unauthenticated login.

checks.title: Verify root account status and lock status
checks.description: On modern Debian/Ubuntu servers, direct root login should be disabled with password locked.

checks.title: Check for non-system accounts with interactive login shells
checks.description: System service accounts should use non-interactive shells like /usr/sbin/nologin or /bin/false.

checks.title: Verify password expiration policy in /etc/login.defs
checks.description: Password maximum age should be configured to 90 days or fewer.

checks.title: Ensure SSH Root Login is disabled
checks.description: Direct remote root login over SSH should be prohibited to enforce non-repudiation.

checks.title: Ensure SSH Password Authentication is restricted
checks.description: Public key authentication should be used instead of passwords where possible.

checks.title: Ensure SSH PermitEmptyPasswords is set to no
checks.description: Disallow login to accounts with empty passwords over SSH.

checks.title: Ensure SSH MaxAuthTries is set to 4 or fewer
checks.description: Limiting authentication attempts mitigates brute-force attacks against SSH.

checks.title: Ensure SSH X11Forwarding is disabled
checks.description: Disabling X11 forwarding prevents GUI hijacking across remote SSH sessions.

checks.title: Ensure SSH Protocol version is strictly 2
checks.description: Legacy SSH version 1 contains known cryptographic weaknesses.

checks.title: Verify permissions and ownership of /etc/passwd
checks.description: /etc/passwd must be owned by root and readable by all, but writable only by root (0644).

checks.title: Verify permissions and ownership of /etc/shadow
checks.description: /etc/shadow stores password hashes and must be restricted to root or shadow group (0640 or 0600).

checks.title: Verify permissions and ownership of /etc/group
checks.description: /etc/group must be owned by root and writable only by root (0644).

checks.title: Verify permissions and ownership of /etc/gshadow
checks.description: /etc/gshadow must be restricted (0640 or 0600).

checks.title: Check for unconfined world-writable files in common paths
checks.description: Files writable by everyone can be modified by unprivileged local attackers.

checks.title: Audit unauthorized SUID/SGID binaries in standard directories
checks.description: SUID binaries execute with superuser privileges and can be exploited for privilege escalation.

checks.title: Ensure host firewall (UFW) is active and running
checks.description: An active firewall blocks unauthorized network packets and prevents service enumeration.

checks.title: Ensure default incoming firewall policy is deny or reject
checks.description: Default ingress policy should drop or reject incoming packets unless explicitly allowed.

checks.title: Ensure SSH port is explicitly allowed before enabling firewall
checks.description: Prevents administrator lockout when activating the firewall.

checks.title: Check for unencrypted legacy service ports listening on all interfaces
checks.description: Legacy services like telnet (23), ftp (21), rsh (514), and http (80) transmit data in cleartext.

checks.title: Verify no network interfaces are operating in promiscuous mode
checks.description: Promiscuous mode indicates packet sniffing or network surveillance activity.

checks.title: Verify kernel sysctl network hardening settings
checks.description: IP forwarding should be disabled and ICMP redirects ignored on non-router hosts.

checks.title: Ensure obsolete services are masked or not installed
checks.description: Legacy daemons like telnetd, rsh-server, vsftpd, and inetd should not run.

checks.title: Check for pending security package updates via package manager
checks.description: Unpatched vulnerabilities in system packages can lead to arbitrary code execution.

checks.title: Check if unattended-upgrades is installed and enabled
checks.description: Automatic security updates ensure critical CVEs are patched in a timely manner.

checks.title: Verify system logging daemon (rsyslog or systemd-journald) is active
checks.description: Continuous event logging is essential for incident response and forensic analysis.

checks.title: Verify auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) is installed and active
checks.description: Auditd provides detailed kernel-level security event logging.

checks.title: Check for excessive failed login attempts in recent auth logs
checks.description: Spikes in failed logins indicate active brute-force or credential stuffing attacks.
